source: CARE Cambodia (Pailin), "TIP Training on Maize Production" / បទដ្ឋានអនុវត្ដបច្ចេកវិទ្យា ផលិតកម្មដំណំពូតក្របម, 2009. Funded by AusAID (ACIMA project), the European Union (Pailin Food Security Program), and ACIAR (CCPMP project).
text:
The goal of planting technique is to avoid having either too many or too few plants per hectare, since both extremes reduce yield. Whether planting by hand or with a machine (seeder), row spacing and hill (plant) spacing should be set to the recommended distances to achieve the best yield.

Two recommended spacing options, both confirmed by a labeled diagram in the source (row spacing verified visually as 0.7 m in both cases):

1) Row spacing 0.7 m x hill spacing 0.5 m, with 2 seeds planted per hole.
2) Row spacing 0.7 m x hill spacing 0.25 m, with 1 seed planted per hole.

Planting depth should be 2-5 cm. The source states that good weed control at every growth stage is essential to ensure high yield.
